witness.note: Leges Henrici primi: Liebermann’s edited Latin text, from the manuscripts he names in Gesetze I, p. 547, note a, listed below
London, The National Archives (formerly the Public Record Office), E 164/2 (the Red Book of the Exchequer)
The original of the London collection, Leges Anglorum Londoniis collectae (c. 1210), which survives in copies
London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius D.ii (Liebermann’s K, also K2)
John Selden’s manuscript, now lost (known from Twysden’s variants)
Roger Twysden, in Wheloc’s edition of Lambarde’s Archaionomia (Cambridge, 1644)
London, Guildhall (Corporation of London), a lost manuscript (there from at least 1639 to 1721), known only from the variants cited by earlier editors as “Lond”
Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Latin 155

div.head: Hn 11.17
div.ab: In causis autem emendabilibus sanctorum miseracione permissum est, ut terreni domini audeant ex eorum licencia peccunialem emendacionem capere secundum legem patrie.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 557 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: Religiöse Begründung weltlicher Justiz erblickt hierin Stubbs (Lect. 156) richtig: doch vielleicht nur für die Quelle, Ælfred, beweiskräftig—12 em.{2} d., que non: besser—12, 1 Ex his—12, 1a Q. eme. n.{6} p., q. besser—þiepe{8} et c. morð et hafordswiche Rs

Stubbs (Lect. 156) rightly sees in this a religious justification of secular justice: but perhaps conclusive only for the source, Ælfred—12 em.{2} d., que non: better—12, 1 Ex his—12, 1a Q. eme. n.{6} p., q. better—þiepe{8} et c. morð et hafordswiche Rs

div.ab: In cases for which compensation can be paid, it has been permitted by the mercy of the saints that earthly lords may venture, by their leave, to take money compensation according to the law of the land.
